statement_blocker: The catalog names Property (T) and gives only a rigidity gloss. It does not state a truth-valued proposition or select the compact-Kazhdan-set definition, the almost-invariant-implies-invariant characterization, Fell-topology isolation, compact generation, a higher-rank example, lattice inheritance, or the Delorme-Guichardet equivalence. It also omits the group domain, topology, continuity/unitarity model, Hilbert-space conventions, ordered binders, compact-subset and positive-constant quantifiers, vector normalization, and boundary cases. Selecting a root at intake would invent or substitute mathematics.
domain_and_universes: Open: the selected source must fix a topological group and universe, any separation/local-compactness/sigma-compactness/countability hypotheses, complex Hilbert spaces and their universes, and strongly continuous unitary representation conventions.
conclusion: Open: the repository names a property but does not choose its defining existential implication, a characterization, a consequence, an example theorem, or an equivalence theorem.
degenerate_case_status: No case is excluded before a proposition is selected; the statement phase must resolve every boundary case in scope-map.md.
candidate_scope_not_credited: a topological group has Property (T) when it admits a compact Kazhdan set
every strongly continuous unitary representation with almost invariant vectors has a nonzero invariant vector
for a locally compact group the trivial representation is isolated in the unitary dual
a locally compact group with Property (T) is compactly generated
specified higher-rank groups and their lattices have Property (T)
for sigma-compact locally compact groups Property (T) is equivalent to Property (FH)
degenerate_cases_to_resolve: trivial, compact, empty-carrier-permitting, and subsingleton groups
zero Hilbert spaces, zero vectors, unit vectors, and scale-invariant vector formulations
empty compact subsets and epsilon equal to zero versus strictly positive epsilon
discrete versus nondiscrete topology and finite versus compact test sets
real versus complex Hilbert spaces and inner-product orientation
excluded_substitutions: Kazhdan-Lusztig polynomials, conjectures, bases, or representation formulas
finite generation, finite abelianization, expanders, ergodicity, spectral gaps, or fixed-point consequences alone
Property (FH), first-cohomology vanishing, or Fell-topology isolation without all required hypotheses and checked equivalence
Property (T) for only finite groups, compact groups, one named matrix group, or a single representation
generic algebraic representation or invariant-submodule infrastructure without continuity, unitarity, almost invariance, and a compact Kazhdan set
a structure or hypothesis storing a Kazhdan pair or the desired implication and a tautological projection
the catalog's untrusted verified label or the discovery probe as source or proof credit
